newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end sharply lower, Rhone drops.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end sharply lower, Rhone drops.

text.p: French shares closed sharply lower on Thursday, in line with an opening fall on Wall Street after a surprise decline in U.S. unemployment claims, dealers said.
Investors are now focusing on Friday's U.S. retail sales and producer price data for interest rate prospects.
Rhone-Poulenc fell sharply on a profit warning after a product recall by Rhone-Poulenc Rorer, while Eurotunnel veered back after recent deep falls.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 11.08 points or 0.52 percent at 2,135.63 while the CAC-40 futures contract was down at 2,138.5 from 2,148 on Wednesday's close.
* Volume was 4.62 billion francs of which 3.29 billion in CAC-40 shares.

* Rhone-Poulenc closed 2.98 percent, or 4.30 francs, at 140.10 after Rhone-Poulenc Rorer said its its Centeon LCC venture with Hoechst was recalling all lots of its albumin products as a precaution against a risk of bacterial infection. Rorer said this would have an effect of reducing the consensus 1996 profit estimate by 10 to 12 percent.
Analysts have said Rhone-Poulenc Rorer is responsible of 55 percent of Rhone-Poulenc's results. Rhone-Poulenc had no comment on the profit effect of the recall.
* Eurotunnel closed two percent higher at 7.65 percent after deep falls since unveiling its debt restructuring deal which is giving near majority control in the company to its creditor banks.
* Cie Generale des Eaux unchanged at 582 francs ahead on next Monday's announcement of first-half results and in wake of Cegetel French telecoms deal.
* Scor up four francs at 205 after successful New York listing which was more than four times oversubscribed.

* Alcatel Alsthom firms 0.58 percent to 449.60, as newspaper Les Echos reports the company is preferred bidder in Thomson SA sale. A finance ministry spokeswoman declined to comment on the report which said the government could announce its decision today.
Lagardere, up 1.20 francs at 129.40, is the sole rival bidder for Thomson

* Havas, down 0.89 percent at 357.80, due to post first-half results this evening. The media group is a bidder in the SFP sale. There was also market talk of a bid for Havas by Belgian businessman Albert Frere.
